1	---
2	name: liu-hao-intent
3	description: "Infer Liu Hao's intent and preferences before building, designing, changing or automating anything for him, and when choosing user-facing wording or asking him questions. Use dated preference evidence and existing specialist guidance to choose an aligned outcome."
4	---
5	
6	# Liu Hao's intent and preferences
7	
8	## Handle everything else and lower friction
9	
10	Liu Hao ([2026-10-09](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/10/09/rollout-2026-10-09T10-50-22-01a12012-2411-78a0-98b1-723e7efd4602.jsonl:214), relayed by the lead): “the general preference is just to lower friction as much as possible. what i want to do is think and problem solve and read about research in my daily life. i want to remove and streamline as much friction out of this as possible.”
11	
12	His clarification ([2026-10-09](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/10/09/rollout-2026-10-09T10-50-22-01a12012-2411-78a0-98b1-723e7efd4602.jsonl:266), relayed by the lead): “you misunderstand - those are things i want to do with my time in general and not something i need from you. the idea is that you handle everything else”.
13	
14	Thinking, problem solving and reading research are his activities. Agents handle the surrounding admin, logistics, tooling, setup, sign-ins and upkeep end to end within the granted authority, so as little as possible reaches him. Leave him the time and attention for what he wants to do.
15	
16	Treat the principles below as consequences: fewer places to check, fewer steps he takes, less text he must read, and agents that finish instead of handing work back. Judge the result by how much routine work and friction it takes off his hands.
17	
18	Use these as evidence-backed defaults. His current request and explicit restrictions win; preferences do not grant permission to spend, send, publish or change unrelated work. Updated 2026-10-09.
19	
20	Infer the outcome behind his words. Repeated corrections and explicit choices carry more weight than generic praise. Keep a choice tied to its context: liking one preview does not make its theme a rule for every project. Read only the existing guidance relevant to the task.
21	
22	## General principles
23	
24	- **Generalise the intent.** Turn examples into a test that also works on new cases; never encode a list of his examples as the rule.
25	  Evidence ([2026-10-08](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-generalise-examples.md)): “generalise from examples i provide rather than just citing those exact examples”.
26	
27	- **Build the simplest robust solution that finishes the job.** Avoid extra layers, switches and process that add work without improving the outcome.
28	  Evidence ([2026-09-30](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md)): “implement the simplest robust solution”.
29	
30	- **Inspect and reuse before adding.** Understand the current setup, related work and owner before creating a replacement or parallel system.
31	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md)): “so they don't duplicate existing work”.
32	
33	- **Keep related work in a place he already checks.** Integrate new sources and surface their results there; avoid another destination or habit to remember.
34	  Evidence ([2026-10-08](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-one-place.md)): “i dont want things scattered around in different locations.”
35	
36	- **Own the routine work.** Complete authorized steps and resolve recurring friction durably; hand back only the part that actually needs him.
37	  Evidence ([2026-10-09](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-automate-blockers.md)): “don't delegate things to me”.
38	
39	- **Stay inside the task.** Solve the full requested problem while preserving unrelated work; propose other improvements separately.
40	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md)): “extremely strict about agents staying within bounds”.
41	
42	- **Write directly and briefly for the audience.** Use ordinary words, put the useful point first, and cut padding, stock assistant phrasing and repeated information.
43	  Evidence ([2026-10-09](../admin-board/SKILL.md)): “very informal and straight to the point”.
44	
45	- **Give UI a considered look and little clutter.** Choose a coherent visual style; include text and controls only when they help the actual task. Preserve useful capabilities.
46	  Evidence ([2026-09-30](/Users/liuhao/.claude/projects/-Users-liuhao/8eeedd17-4478-43ac-9072-a193ea21219f.jsonl:2782)): “make the design richer, but also make the actual text concise and straight to the point”.
47	
48	- **Judge content as its intended reader would.** Keep internal instructions and provenance out of finished user-facing material unless that reader needs them; retain citations where the task calls for them.
49	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-form-reader-review.md)): “think about it from the perspective of the person reading the form”.
50	
51	- **Make necessary questions plain.** When his decision is genuinely needed, describe what changes for him in everyday language; settle implementation choices yourself.
52	  Evidence ([2026-09-01](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/feedback-plain-language-questions.md)): “Keep the questions less technical and more ELI5”.
53	
54	- **Batch real decisions.** Gather the few answers that change the outcome together, reuse answers already given, and avoid repeated check-ins.
55	  Evidence ([2026-09-23](/Users/liuhao/.claude/projects/-Users-liuhao/54b8f0da-d459-4820-824f-49439a696d3f.jsonl:740), selected answer): “Ask me here in batches”.
56	
57	- **Verify usable results.** Check the actual saved artifact or working behaviour against the requested outcome before calling it done.
58	  Evidence ([2026-10-03](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/10/03/rollout-2026-10-03T23-49-07-01a103f4-f3ad-74c1-b99b-4b49506152e9.jsonl:819)): “test this and dont stop until it works viably”.
59	
60	- **Keep automation light and preserve other work.** Consider everyday responsiveness and shared resources, as well as whether the automation itself works.
61	  Evidence ([2026-08-11](/Users/liuhao/.codex/sessions/2026/08/11/rollout-2026-08-11T00-13-04-019fedf3-77fc-7d62-bb96-fab1be6e7d2a.jsonl:1491)): “don't want it to slow down my computer”.
62	
63	## Before you build
64	
65	- Does this take routine work off his hands, or add a chore before he can use his time as he wants?
66	- What outcome would he notice, where would he find it, and what would prove it works?
67	- What did he explicitly request or forbid, and what am I merely assuming?
68	- What already serves this purpose? Inspect it and the relevant feedback before proposing another system.
69	- What has he rejected in this area, and what general preference explains that rejection?
70	- What is the simplest complete solution with the least extra reading, clutter and manual work for him?
71	- Can I settle this from his instructions, existing setup and past choices instead of asking him?
72	- Read the proposed result as its real audience, and check the actual experience before reporting completion.
73	
74	## Defaults for the surrounding work
75	
76	Apply these without a preference questionnaire (2026-10-09 clarification):
77	
78	- Show the useful result where he already looks; keep tool details behind it rather than creating another place he must visit.
79	- Background jobs must never slow what he is doing. Throttle, pause or wait for idle time automatically; his active work takes priority.
80	- Make small, helpful, reversible changes within the requested task and tell him afterwards. Preserve unrelated work and separately required approvals.
81	- Reuse the existing look and familiar interactions. Keep common actions easy to reach and secondary controls out of the way; choose sensible details yourself.
82	- Finish the workflow, including routine setup, sign-in recovery and upkeep within the task. Bring him only the part that genuinely needs his decision or presence.
83	
84	## When to ask
85	
86	First inspect available records, existing authenticated sessions and tools, and try a targeted routine recovery. Finish independent authorized work before bringing a question.
87	
88	Ask him only for a real decision or human-only step, never for a preference you can infer. This includes a consequential choice outside the granted authority, confirmation required at action time, an essential personal fact unavailable from his records, or verified MFA, CAPTCHA or Touch ID. Ordinary reversible work within the task needs no new approval.
89	
90	Batch real decisions; give 2–4 short options that say what happens for him, with a recommendation where useful. For a human-only blocker, name the service/app, attempted step, observed obstacle and smallest action needed. Show concrete alternatives only for a real visual decision you cannot infer; do not ask him to invent a design.
91	
92	Infer preferences, never consent or personal facts. Read the applicable live spending cap before any paid step.
93	
94	## Reuse existing guidance
95	
96	- [Write like Liu Hao](../write-like-liu-hao/SKILL.md): text written on his behalf; choose the audience's register rather than making everything casual.
97	- [Admin board](../admin-board/SKILL.md): current admin destinations and inclusion rules; do not copy its particular items into general rules.
98	- [Asking Liu Hao](../overseer/references/asking-liu-hao.md) and [worker checkpoints](../overseer/references/worker-checkpoints.md): blocker handling, scope and worker briefs.
99	- [Feedback notes](../../projects/-Users-liuhao/memory/): consult relevant preference notes; treat old operational instructions as historical evidence when current instructions differ.
100	- [Machine automations](../machine-automations/SKILL.md): existing mechanisms before building or changing an automation; every new one joins the others as one ecosystem (its "Build into the ecosystem" rule). [Direct-answer gate](../../hooks/direct-answer-gate.py): existing reply checks; reuse its criteria without adding another gate or invoking a paid check without authorization.

1	---
2	name: running-ceridwen-experiments
3	description: Configure and run Ceridwen fits on Vast.ai, retrieve results, and verify local artifacts. Add analysis or wiki reports only when requested.
4	---
5	
6	# Run one Ceridwen experiment
7	
8	## Default scope: fit and retrieve
9	
10	A request to run or try a fit means configure, run, retrieve, validate, and report.
11	Prioritise a working fit and reliable local results. Do not create an experiment
12	write-up, separate analysis notebook, extra plots, wiki page, or prose-review task
13	unless the user requests that deliverable. Existing notebook plots still run.
14	Do not delay launch or retrieval for documentation or a documentation-only commit.
15	
16	Read `AGENTS.md`. For a quick fit, the configuration, pinned source, seed, manifest,
17	stage logs, and result files are the reproducibility record. Keep only a short
18	Beads status with the output path and any blocker. Read `wiki/research/README.md`
19	only if research records or wiki publication are part of the request.
20	
21	New runs use the compact dependency image pinned in `scripts/vast.py`, selected
22	input files, and cached grids. Do not replace it with a generic CUDA image.
23	Use `--image` only for an explicitly requested override. Saved runs keep their image.
24	
25	## Production defaults
26	
27	The production defaults are `SETTINGS` and `PRIORS` in
28	`notebooks/ceridwen_integrated_photometry_spectra.ipynb`. An `experiment.json` that
29	omits a key runs with the notebook value. `python3 scripts/ceridwen_state.py` prints
30	each value with the records that tested it (skill `checking-ceridwen-state`).
31	
32	Liu Hao, 2026-09-30, on the nebular grid with line marginalisation and the Ca II K,
33	Ca II H and Ca I mask: "this seems like a good default". On [O II], Hβ and [O III]:
34	"keep o unmasked as default is fine". On `diffuse_Ebump`: "for bump, keep prior (0, 6)".
35	On metallicity evolution: "the metallicity-evolution slope (ZH beta, the zevo arm of
36	wiki/research/experiments/e-dust-bump.md) should be part of the production default".
37	On this section: "make sure all the defaults are well saved in apporpriate skillsl, wiki etc".
38	
39	The M1_210210 configs of 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30 under `results/` set
40	`diffuse_Ebump` to `Uniform(low=0.0, high=12.0)`; their records state it. The notebook
41	default is `Uniform(low=0.0, high=6.0)`.
42	
43	## Steps
44	
45	1. **Configure.** Write `experiment.json` in the experiment's result directory.
46	   Use the production notebook's `SETTINGS` and `PRIORS` keys. Do not edit its
47	   defaults to configure an experiment. Example:
48	   ```json
49	   {
50	     "targets": ["M1_210210"],
51	     "seed": 20260832,
52	     "settings": {},
53	     "priors": {},
54	     "arms": {
55	       "baseline": {},
56	       "wide_dust": {"priors": {"diffuse_tau_noll": "Uniform(low=0.0, high=2.0)"}}
57	     }
58	   }
59	   ```
60	   Each arm merges its changes into the shared settings and priors. Nested
61	   settings merge too. Priors are Python expression strings. `settings.ssp_grid`
62	   accepts a registered name or a local `.h5` path relative to this JSON file.
63	   The exact seed applies to every fit. New model code must be committed before
64	   running; the command uses committed HEAD and pinned submodules.
65	2. **Check.** Use `--dry-run` to check the configuration and local inputs without
66	   rentals or network access. It requires cached grids. Show the targets, changes,
67	   baseline and cap if those choices still need the user's approval. Existing
68	   authorization covers execution; do not ask for the same approval again.
69	3. **Run.** Use this command for new experiment fits:
70	   ```bash
71	   python3 scripts/experiment.py run results/<slug>/experiment.json \
72	     --gpu "RTX 5090" --output results/<slug>/run
73	   ```
74	   Use the GPU type requested by the user. Offers must have reliability above
75	   99.5%, falling back to above 96% only if no offers pass all filters. Both
76	   bandwidth rates must be below $10/TB. The total $1 cap covers all arms and
77	   retries; `--spend-cap` can reduce it.
78	   The runner ranks offers by the latest row for each host in `scripts/vast_hosts.csv`:
79	   `good`, then no row, then `poor`. It rents a `poor` host only when no other offer
80	   passes the filters. In the same group, it rents the lowest cost per fit. It gets
81	   the cost per fit from the `calls/s` value of the host. A host without a `calls/s`
82	   value gets the median value for the GPU type, so among such hosts the lowest
83	   hourly price wins.
84	
85	   Missing registered grids download locally before rental. The command uploads
86	   pinned source and checked grids, runs the full notebook with figure
87	   construction skipped on the box (CERIDWEN_PLOTS=0; figures render nothing
88	   under Agg), downloads each arm-target result, destroys its rental, and then
89	   rebuilds the standard figures locally while keeping the GPU-computed
90	   derived outputs.
91	   Results are under `run/fits/<arm>/<object>-<target>/`: executed notebook,
92	   `ceridwen_result.h5`, derived outputs and logs. The run directory also holds
93	   the manifest, stage logs and available charges. Repeat the same command and
94	   `--output` to resume its source, configuration, completed fits and budget.
95	   Do not manually rent replacements. The historical arm-specific runners remain
96	   for their existing runs.
97	4. **Verify retrieval.** Check every requested arm and target in the local
98	   manifest against `run/fits/`. Run `scripts.experiment.validate_result` locally
99	   on each result directory using `ceridwen/.venv/bin/python`. It opens the result
100	   HDF5, checks finite weights and evidence, checks derived groups and diagnostics,
101	   and checks the executed notebook for errors. Confirm the logs were retrieved.
102	   A remote success message or an existing filename is not enough.
103	
104	   If retrieval or validation fails, preserve the partial files and logs. Diagnose
105	   whether the fit, post-processing, or transfer failed. Recover available outputs
106	   before considering another paid fit. Resume through the runner with the same
107	   configuration and output directory, within the remaining cap. Do not delete
108	   completed results or blindly rerun the sampler to repair missing plots.
109	5. **Record hosts.** List the hosts that started an instance:
110	   ```bash
111	   python3 -c "import json; [print(a['offer']['host_id'], a['offer']['gpu_name'], a['status'], a.get('error', '')) for a in json.load(open('results/<slug>/run/manifest.json'))['attempts'] if a.get('instance_id')]"
112	   ```
113	   Add one row for each host to the end of `scripts/vast_hosts.csv`, with the
114	   columns `host_id,outcome,gpu,date,run,reason`. The latest row sets the outcome.
115	   - Write `good` when the fit finished on the host.
116	   - Write `poor` when the host failed. Examples: the boot stalled, the instance
117	     became unavailable, or the host closed SSH.
118	   - Do not add a row for an offer that did not start an instance.
119	   - Do not add a row for a failure that our code or inputs caused.
120	   - Do not add a row when the records do not show the cause.
121	6. **Finish.** Report success or partial failure, the local result path, and any
122	   diagnostic failure in 2–3 lines. Link the existing executed notebook and result
123	   file. Commit and push task-owned configuration, code and new host rows as
124	   required by `AGENTS.md`.
125	   Once local results are verified, the quick-fit task is complete.
126	
127	## Analysis and publication: only when requested
128	
129	If the user asks for analysis, comparisons, new figures, or a wiki report, produce
130	only those requested outputs after retrieval. Follow `wiki/research/README.md` and
131	the relevant plotting or wiki skill for that work. An explicit request for a full
132	experiment record still includes the record. Do not infer that request from
133	“experiment”, “try”, or “run a fit”. Documentation must not delay result retrieval.
134	
135	Local SSH errors stop before rental. Use an execution environment authorized to run
136	SSH; waiting for the GPU cannot fix a local user-ID error. The shared upload
137	includes HST cutouts and the emission-line table. A nonzero remote stage exit
138	saves its log, destroys the owned rental and stops. Diagnose the log before
139	repeating the command; do not rent a replacement for the same code or input error.
140	
141	### Standard figures for a result page
142	
143	Liu Hao, 2026-09-29: "i just want my usual corner plots, sfh against time etc in
144	accordance with the standard wiki". Put these figures on the page, in this order.
145	Do not design a different figure.
146	
147	| Order | Figure | Wiki file | Source |
148	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
149	| 1 | Spectrum fit: fitted LEGA-C pixels, posterior median, 16-84% band, pulls | `spectrum-<arm>-<target>.png` | `cell14_2.png` |
150	| 2 | Photometry fit: band fluxes, model medians, median continuum, pulls | `photometry-<arm>-<target>.png` | `cell14_1.png` |
151	| 3 | SFH of one fit: normalized SFR against lookback time, median, 16-84% band | `sfh-<arm>-<target>.png` | `cell20_7.png` |
152	| 4 | SFH of all arms on the same axes, and the mass fraction younger | `sfh-<target>.png` | `analysis.ipynb` |
153	| 5 | Corner of the physical parameters of one fit | `corner-<arm>-<target>.png` | `cell20_5.png` |
154	| 6 | Corner of all arms on the same axes, 1σ contours | `corner-<target>.png` | `analysis.ipynb` |
155	
156	Show figures 1 and 2 for each arm before figure 3. Figures 4 and 6 are only for a
157	comparison of fits. The rules are in `wiki/AGENTS.md`, "Result reporting", and in
158	`AGENTS.md`, "Repository and reproducibility conventions". Read them.
159	
160	The commands are from the M1_210210 KC13-bump page of 2026-09-29:
161	`wiki/notes/m1-210210-kcbump.md`, with figures in `wiki/analyses/m1-210210-kcbump/`.
162	
163	1. **Get the figures of each fit.** The production notebook made them during the fit
164	   with `scripts/spectral_figures.py`. Do not run the fit again. This command writes
165	   each saved image of the executed notebook to `<dir>/cell<cell>_<count>.png`:
166	   ```bash
167	   ceridwen/.venv/bin/python - \
168	     results/<slug>/run/fits/<arm>/<object>-<target>/<target>_executed.ipynb <dir> <<'EOF'
169	   import base64, sys
170	   import nbformat
171	   nb = nbformat.read(sys.argv[1], as_version=4)
172	   k = 0
173	   for i, c in enumerate(nb.cells):
174	       for o in c.get("outputs", []):
175	           if "image/png" in o.get("data", {}):
176	               open(f"{sys.argv[2]}/cell{i:02d}_{k}.png", "wb").write(base64.b64decode(o["data"]["image/png"]))
177	               k += 1
178	   EOF
179	   ```
180	   Cell 14 is the notebook section "Output fit". Cell 20 is "Corners and SFH". Open
181	   each image before you copy it. A different notebook version can change the names.
182	2. **Make the comparison figures.** Copy `results/m1-210210-kcbump-2026-09-29/analysis.ipynb`
183	   to `results/<slug>/analysis.ipynb`. In code cell 1, set `RESULTS`, `TARGET`, `FIT_DIRS`,
184	   `COLOURS`, `NAMES` and `REF`. The baseline arm has the colour `#222222`. Then run:
185	   ```bash
186	   PYTHONPATH="$PWD/external/sedpy_jax" ceridwen/.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
187	   import nbformat
188	   from nbclient import NotebookClient
189	   p = "results/<slug>/analysis.ipynb"
190	   nb = nbformat.read(p, as_version=4)
191	   try:
192	       NotebookClient(nb, timeout=None, kernel_name="python3",
193	                      resources={"metadata": {"path": "results/<slug>"}}).execute()
194	   finally:
195	       nbformat.write(nb, p)
196	   EOF
197	   ```
198	   The notebook reads the saved results of each arm. It writes `sfh-<target>.png`,
199	   `corner-<target>.png` and `comparison.csv` to `results/<slug>/`.
200	3. **Copy the figures to the wiki.**
201	   ```bash
202	   D=wiki/analyses/<slug> && mkdir -p $D
203	   cp <dir>/cell14_2.png $D/spectrum-<arm>-<target>.png
204	   cp <dir>/cell14_1.png $D/photometry-<arm>-<target>.png
205	   cp <dir>/cell20_7.png $D/sfh-<arm>-<target>.png
206	   cp <dir>/cell20_5.png $D/corner-<arm>-<target>.png
207	   cp results/<slug>/sfh-<target>.png results/<slug>/corner-<target>.png $D/
208	   ```
209	   For an arm that has figures on a different wiki page, use those files.
210	4. **Check each figure at 900 px.** Run
211	   `sips --resampleWidth 900 <file> --out <dir>/<name>_900.png`. Then open the output.
212	5. **Write the page.** Use the `editing-the-wiki` skill. Use the structure of
213	   `wiki/notes/m1-210210-kcbump.md`.
214	6. **Put the page on the wiki Results page.** Liu Hao, 2026-09-29: "i don't see it in
215	   results. always put this stuff in results". Link the page from the research record
216	   of the experiment in `wiki/research/experiments/`. The example is
217	   `wiki/research/experiments/e-dust-bump.md`:
218	   ```yaml
219	   source_notes: m1-210210-kcbump
220	   result_groups: results/m1-210210-kcbump-2026-09-29
221	   ```
222	   `source_notes` is the slug of the note. `result_groups` is the result directory.
223	   For the other fields, read `wiki/research/README.md`. Then run:
224	   ```bash
225	   python3 wiki/build.py
226	   python3 wiki/tests/run_tests.py
227	   python3 -m unittest discover -s wiki/tests -p 'test_research.py'
228	   ```
229	   Commit and push the record. Then check the live Results page:
230	   ```bash
231	   ssh truenas 'curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/results/' < /dev/null | grep <record id>
232	   ```
233	   If there is no output, wait 10 seconds and do the check again. If there is no
234	   output after 60 seconds, the record is not on the page. Find the cause.
235	
236	The executed notebook has more images. Add one only when the request names it.
237	
238	| Image | Notebook section | Figure |
239	| --- | --- | --- |
240	| `cell04_0.png` | Data and target | HST ACS F814W cutout with the 3 arcsec aperture |
241	| `cell16_3.png` | Spectrum fit | Spectrum fit on all valid native pixels, excluded pixels in grey |
242	| `cell18_4.png` | Calibration polynomial | Calibration polynomial, median and 16-84% band |
243	| `cell20_6.png` | Corners and SFH | Corner of the dust parameters against the SFH mass fractions |
244	| `cell22_8.png` | Prior-to-posterior KL | KL divergence from prior to posterior for each parameter, in bits |
245	
246	An old executed notebook can lack `cell20_6.png`. Make it from the saved posterior:
247	`ceridwen/.venv/bin/python scripts/add_dust_sfh_corner.py <result dir> --png <file>`.

| Part | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Value, `what` | `SETTINGS` or `PRIORS` in `notebooks/ceridwen_integrated_photometry_spectra.ipynb`, and the comment there |
| `off`, `production default` | The value. `False` and `None` are `off`. |
| `built`, `changed` | The notebook commits that added the entry or changed its value or comment |
| `code` | The Ceridwen commits that those notebook commits pinned, and later commits to the files they created |
| `tested`, `planned`, `running`, `stopped` | A record in `wiki/research/experiments/` with the entry in `features`. The text is its `finding`. The state word is its `status`. |
| `ran` | An `experiment.json` in `results/` that changed the entry: record or directory, arm, value |
| `open` | The question of each such record, if the question is not `answered` |

## The blocks of the output

1. `SETTINGS` and `PRIORS`: one entry for each key.
2. `MODEL OPTIONS`: each option of `CSPBasis_afe`, and each option that only `CSPBasis`
   has. On 2026-09-30, `add_neb` was `[not in CSPBasis_afe; CSPBasis has it, default True]`.
3. `FEATURES THAT ARE NOT A CURRENT NOTEBOOK KEY OR CLASS OPTION`: a name in `features`
   that is not in blocks 1 and 2, with the commit that removed it from the notebook.
4. `WORK THAT IS NOT MERGED`: each branch that HEAD or the pinned Ceridwen does not
   contain, and each other worktree with changes that are not committed.
5. `OPEN ISSUES`: the `bd` issues that are open or in progress.
6. `EXPERIMENT RECORDS`: planned, running, or with results from the last 14 days.
   `--days 3` changes the 14. With a text, all records are candidates.
7. `RUN DIRECTORIES IN NO RECORD`: each `results/` directory with an `experiment.json`
   and a run manifest that no record lists in `result_groups`. A quick fit is here.
8. With a text only: the newest commits and the `wiki/research` files that contain it.

## Keep the records current

When you write or change an experiment record, set these two lines in its front matter.
The command shows a record under a feature only through them.

```yaml
features: emission_line_marginalisation
finding: M1_210210, on minus off: mass-weighted age -0.408 Gyr; RMS pull within 300 km/s of Hbeta 0.568 off, 0.484 on; ln Z not comparable with masked fits
```

- `features`: the names that the run used, with commas between them.
- `finding`: one line. Copy each number from the section Results of the record.

## Limits of the output

- A `finding` is a short copy. Read the section Results of the record before you speak
  about the result.
- A record without `features` is not under a feature. Find it with the text:
  `python3 scripts/ceridwen_state.py <text>`.
- `$ invoiced` is the sum of the `charges.json` files that `scripts/experiment.py`
  saved. A directory without `charges.json` shows no amount. Its record gives the cost.
- The command does not print `abandoned`. A record that stopped shows `stopped`. A
  branch shows the date of its last commit.

## Related rules

- For priorities and direction, read `AGENTS.md`, section "Research priorities".
- To run a fit, use the `running-ceridwen-experiments` skill.
- For the fields of a record, read `wiki/research/README.md`.

        raise ValueError('configuration overrides must be objects')
    result = dict(base)
    for key, value in changes.items():
        if key not in base:
            raise ValueError(f'unknown configuration key: {key}')
        result[key] = merge(base[key], value) if isinstance(base[key], dict) else value
    return result
